# train RF model. 

```{r}
library(randomForest)
basedir <- "/projectnb/dietzelab/dongchen/SDA_disturbance/example_polygon/downscale_dist_DA/"
rf.train.downscale <- function(dat.train, predictor) {
  # 1. Ensure the predictor exists in the dataset
  if (!(predictor %in% colnames(dat.train))) {
    stop(paste("Predictor", predictor, "not found in the training data."))
  }
  
  # 2. Dynamically create the formula (e.g., agb ~ .)
  # This uses all other columns in dat.train as independent variables
  form <- as.formula(paste(predictor, "~ ."))
  
  # 3. Train the Random Forest model
  # na.action = na.fail is standard, but complete.cases are already handled in your prep
  message(paste("Training Random Forest model for:", predictor))
  rf.model <- randomForest(
    formula = form,
    data = dat.train,
    ntree = 1000,       # Standard default, adjust based on performance/time
    importance = TRUE  # Keeps track of variable importance
  )
  
  return(rf.model)
}

rf.predict.downscale <- function(dat.pred, rf.model, chunk_size = 50000, n_cores = 30) {
  library(parallel)
  
  # 1. Verify the model is valid
  if (!inherits(rf.model, "randomForest")) {
    stop("The provided rf.model is not a valid randomForest object.")
  }
  
  # 2. Identify and filter covariates expected by the model
  model_vars <- rownames(rf.model$importance)
  if (!all(model_vars %in% colnames(dat.pred))) {
    missing <- model_vars[!model_vars %in% colnames(dat.pred)]
    stop(paste("Prediction data is missing required covariates:", paste(missing, collapse = ", ")))
  }
  dat.pred_subset <- dat.pred[, model_vars, drop = FALSE]
  
  n_rows <- nrow(dat.pred_subset)
  message(paste("Starting parallel downscale prediction for", n_rows, "rows using", n_cores, "cores..."))
  
  # 3. Define the chunk indices
  start_indices <- seq(1, n_rows, by = chunk_size)
  
  # 4. Run predictions in parallel across chunks
  pred_list <- mclapply(start_indices, function(start_idx) {
    end_idx <- min(start_idx + chunk_size - 1, n_rows)
    
    # Predict for this specific chunk
    predict(
      object = rf.model, 
      newdata = dat.pred_subset[start_idx:end_idx, , drop = FALSE]
    )
  }, mc.cores = n_cores)
  
  # 5. Combine results back into a single numeric vector
  pred_results <- unlist(pred_list)
  
  message("Parallel prediction complete!")
  return(pred_results)
}

pred.2.map <- function(preds, lats, lons, r_template) {
  library(terra)
  
  # 1. Create a data frame from coordinates and predicted values
  # Assumes preds, lats, and lons are aligned vectors of the same length
  df <- data.frame(lon = lons, lat = lats, value = preds)
  
  # 2. Convert the data frame to a SpatVector object (points)
  # Crds specifies the column names for longitude and latitude
  # crs = crs(r_template) ensures the projection matches your target raster
  pts_spatial <- vect(df, geom = c("lon", "lat"), crs = crs(r_template))
  
  # 3. Rasterize the points onto the template raster grid
  # fun = mean handles cases where multiple points fall into one cell, 
  # though if they align perfectly, it simply maps the values.
  r_mapped <- rasterize(pts_spatial, r_template, field = "value", fun = mean)
  
  return(r_mapped)
}
# take 2024 for example.
# basic info.
ref_dem <- terra::rast("/projectnb/dietzelab/dongchen/SDA_disturbance/dem_merged/dem_resample.tif")
dod.shp <- terra::vect("/projectnb/dietzelab/dongchen/SDA_disturbance/selected_polygons/selected_polygons.shp")
r_template <- terra::rast(terra::crop(ref_dem, dod.shp[3,]))
years <- 2001:2024
t <- 24
ens <- 1
# loop over years.
for (t in 1:24) {
  dir.create(file.path(basedir, years[t]))
# loop over variables for each ensemble.
for (ens in 1:50) {
  analysis.t.agb <- as.numeric(analysis.all[[t]][ens, seq(1, 4*length(pts), 4)])
  dat.train <- cbind(analysis.t.agb, attribute.table)
  model <- rf.train.downscale(dat.train, "analysis.t.agb")
  pred <- rf.predict.downscale(dat, model)
  agb.rast <- pred.2.map(pred, dat$lat, dat$lon, r_template)
  # terra::plot(agb.rast, main = "2024 AGB (Mg/ha)")

  analysis.t.lai <- as.numeric(analysis.all[[t]][ens, seq(2, 4*length(pts), 4)])
  dat.train <- cbind(analysis.t.lai, attribute.table)
  model <- rf.train.downscale(dat.train, "analysis.t.lai")
  pred <- rf.predict.downscale(dat, model)
  lai.rast <- pred.2.map(pred, dat$lat, dat$lon, r_template)
  # terra::plot(lai.rast, main = "2024 LAI (m2/m2)")
  
  analysis.t.sm <- as.numeric(analysis.all[[t]][ens, seq(3, 4*length(pts), 4)])
  dat.train <- cbind(analysis.t.sm, attribute.table)
  model <- rf.train.downscale(dat.train, "analysis.t.sm")
  pred <- rf.predict.downscale(dat, model)
  sm.rast <- pred.2.map(pred, dat$lat, dat$lon, r_template)
  
  analysis.t.soc <- as.numeric(analysis.all[[t]][ens, seq(4, 4*length(pts), 4)])
  dat.train <- cbind(analysis.t.soc, attribute.table)
  model <- rf.train.downscale(dat.train, "analysis.t.soc")
  pred <- rf.predict.downscale(dat, model)
  soc.rast <- pred.2.map(pred, dat$lat, dat$lon, r_template)
  
  rast.all.ens <- c(agb.rast, lai.rast, sm.rast, soc.rast)
  names(rast.all.ens) <- c("AGB", "LAI", "SM", "SOC")
  terra::writeRaster(rast.all.ens, file.path(basedir, years[t], paste0("ens_", ens, ".tif")))
}
}
```
